blocks.content: Blue-green deployment is not a native Kubernetes feature, it is a pattern you build using two complete, separate Deployments and a single Service switch, cutting over all traffic at once, with instant rollback available.

"Blue" and "green" refer to two entirely separate, fully running Deployments, blue is whatever is currently live, green is the new version, deployed fully and completely before any real traffic ever reaches it.

blocks.alt: Two full, independent environments, not one Deployment being updated in place

blocks.content: Unlike rolling update and Recreate, both native strategy options on a Deployment, blue-green is a pattern you construct yourself out of ordinary Kubernetes primitives, nothing marks a Deployment as "blue" or "green" in any special way.

blocks.alt: A pattern you build, not a strategy field Kubernetes provides directly

blocks.content: The actual cutover uses the Service selector mechanism covered in the Services module, once green is fully deployed and verified, you switch the Service's selector to point at green's Pods instead of blue's, moving every bit of traffic over instantly, in a single change.

blocks.alt: A single, atomic switch, moving every request over at the exact same moment

blocks.content:
# Before: selector matches the blue deployment
kubectl patch service my-app -p '{"spec":{"selector":{"version":"green"}}}'
# All traffic now goes to green, instantly

codes.bash:
# Before: selector matches the blue deployment
kubectl patch service my-app -p '{"spec":{"selector":{"version":"green"}}}'
# All traffic now goes to green, instantly

blocks.content: This is blue-green's standout advantage over rolling update, if something goes wrong after cutover, reverting is exactly as instant as the cutover itself, switch the selector back to blue, which never stopped running the whole time.

blocks.alt: A genuinely instant reversal, blue never stopped running in the background

blocks.content: 5. The Real Cost: Double the Resources
blocks.text: 5. The Real Cost: Double the Resources

blocks.content: This capability is not free, both environments run fully, simultaneously, for the duration of the cutover window, meaning genuinely double the compute resources temporarily, a real cost weighed against the safety and instant-rollback benefit it buys.

blocks.alt: A genuine, temporary doubling of resource cost, the real price of this safety

blocks.title: Key Takeaway
points: Blue-green is a pattern built from two full Deployments and a Service selector switch, not a native Kubernetes feature, cutting over all traffic instantly.
It offers genuinely instant rollback, since the old version never stops running, at the real, temporary cost of doubled resource usage during the cutover.
